# The generated coverage matrix

**Generated by `tools/coverage/` (the `coverage` target). Do not edit: the next run
overwrites it.**

The question this file turns into a number: *what can we not compare?* It is emitted by a
tool rather than written by hand so that adding a product to this repository moves the
matrix without anyone remembering to.

## 0. What is live and what is a snapshot

| side | status |
|---|---|
| **Epykos (ours)** | **LIVE.** Instrument kinds, coupon mechanics, curve schemes and curve variables are discovered from the shipped enums at run time; conventions, blueprints, curve definitions and the Stage A problem are loaded from `blueprints/` through the engine's own loaders; the head-to-head's reach is read off `fixtures::compare_ois` by building it. **No product is named by hand on this side.** |
| **SwapEngine (theirs)** | **SNAPSHOT, dated 2026-10-09.** A checked-in table. Every row carries the file and the symbol it was read from so it can be re-verified in seconds. It can go stale, and nothing in this repository will notice if it does. |

Their checkout, for re-verification: `/Users/kevinbroughton/Desktop/Claude Projects/SwapEngine`.

Reading it is permitted (D11 as relaxed by the owner, 2026-10-09). **Copying it is not**, and nothing here is copied: this is an inventory of which symbols
exist in which file, not of what they do. The clean-room property is exactly what makes a
head-to-head mean anything -- if we absorbed their implementation the comparison would
measure nothing.

### The three levels

A two-way *both / theirs only* verdict is the wrong shape, because it hides the distinction
that drives planning. Every row below is exactly one of:

| level | meaning |
|---|---|
| **both, compared** | the head-to-head exercises it **today**. This is the number that bounds what any current measurement can say. |
| both, *not compared* | the engine and the blueprints have it; the head-to-head does not reach it. A **fixture** gap, not a capability gap -- the cheap half of the ranked list. |
| **theirs only** | no path to it here at all. A **capability** gap. |

Folding *not compared* into "both" overstates what we can measure; folding it into "theirs
only" understates what we have built.

| `Portfolio` | `include/swaps/calibration/problem.hpp`<br>enum class QuoteKind (:64), :81 | a weighted combination of nested instruments quoted as one number | **theirs only** | -- |

| `Npv` | `include/swaps/calibration/problem.hpp`<br>enum class QuoteKind (:64), :93 | a position's net present value as the quote, in PV units | **theirs only** | -- |

**What it would take**, for the *theirs only* rows:

- **`ZeroCouponRate`** -- A transform of a quote we already compute, not new maths: `exp(log(1+tau*q)/tau) - 1` is expressible in the current op set (`Op::Exp`, `Op::Log`) and **no `Op::Pow` is needed**. The real obstacle is structural -- a quote CONVENTION is not something our types carry (see the fused-axis finding) -- so it lands as a residual wrapper plus one blueprint field.
- **`FxForward`** -- Blocked on Stage B, not on a small change: `blueprints/problems/stage_a.json`'s own notes fix the USD conversion of EUR values at a placeholder of 1.0 recorded as `fx.placeholder`, and say Stage B replaces it with an FX spot INPUT. Needs an FX spot as a tape input, a second discount curve in the residual, and a reporting-currency conversion that is a recorded product rather than a constant.
- **`XccyMtmBasis`** -- Everything `FxForward` needs, plus a resetting-notional funding leg -- a coupon mechanic `instrument::CouponKind` has no member for. Strictly behind `FxForward`.
- **`Portfolio`** -- Cheap, and it needs no engine maths: `solver::CurveSet::add_instrument` already takes an arbitrary callable residual, so a weighted sum of component residuals is expressible today. Missing: a blueprint shape that NESTS instruments (theirs compose recursively, `std::vector<WeightedInstrument>`) and a quote key for the combination.
- **`TurnJump`** -- **Not a new interpolation scheme**, which is the natural guess and is wrong. Theirs is an ADDITIVE OVERLAY with its own unknown: one free delta per turn appended to the state vector AFTER the interpolation knots (`CurveStructure::turns`, `n_knots() = n_interp_knots() + turns.size()`), with a closed-form window overlap, so the Jacobian row is a unit vector. For us that is a state-vector extension plus a curve overlay term -- `curve::Composite` regions stay untouched. Cheaper than a scheme, but it does widen the unknown vector, which the IFT ladder and the adjoint both see.
- **`Npv`** -- Nearly free in the maths: `instrument::pv<Scalar>` already exists templated on Scalar, so the residual is `pv - target` with no new op. Two wrinkles: the same missing quote-key degree of freedom as `Portfolio`, and **theirs is in PV units while every residual here is in rate units** by deliberate design (so `solve_tol` means one thing everywhere), so the row needs a per-instrument residual scale the solver does not currently have.

### Our side of this axis, live

`instrument::Kind` has **5** live enumerators (`ois`, `irs`, `basis`, `deposit`, `future`); `instrument::CouponKind` has **4** (`fixed`, `rfr_compounded`, `rfr_averaged`, `term_rate`).

| our `Kind` | the quote it calibrates on | answers their | caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ois` | par rate: float leg PV / fixed leg annuity | `ParRate` | -- |
| `irs` | par rate: float leg PV / fixed leg annuity | `ParRate` | -- |
| `basis` | par spread over the flat leg, on the spread leg's annuity | `ParSpread` | -- |
| `deposit` | the index forward over the period | `Rate` | no convexity term, and none is due |
| `future` | price 100(1-rate); residual in rate units | `Rate` | convexity adjustment is ZERO, a stated simplification (D35) |

### The finding that changes the shape of this axis: our two axes are FUSED and theirs are not

Their `QuoteKind` says how a number is *quoted*; the instrument it is quoted on is separate
data. Ours has no such degree of freedom: `instrument::residual` switches on `Kind` and each
kind hard-codes exactly one quote form (`instrument::par` for `Ois`, `Irs`, `Basis` and
`Deposit`; `futures_settlement_rate` for `Future`). So we cannot quote an OIS as a
`ZeroCouponRate` or as an `Npv` even though we price the OIS perfectly well.

That reframes three of the six *theirs only* rows. `ZeroCouponRate`, `Portfolio` and `Npv`
are **not three products we lack** -- they are one missing degree of freedom, a quote
convention per calibration instrument, which `solver::CurveSet::add_instrument` is already
general enough to accept because it takes an arbitrary callable residual. Add the soft-quote
band row from axis 3 and it is four rows behind one change.

A second correction worth recording: **neither engine models futures convexity.** Their
`Rate` takes `convexity` as an input double and their convexity model lives in their tests,
not their engine; ours is zero by the stated simplification of D35. So the two agree exactly
when their convexity input is set to zero -- `Rate` is a *fixture* step, not a maths gap.

**What it would take**, for the *theirs only* rows:

- **`Cross-currency`** -- Blocked on Stage B's FX spot input. The curve-stack half already exists (Stage A is 2 currencies); the FX half does not exist at all.
- **`Inflation`** -- Needs a new index TYPE before any instrument: `conventions::IndexDef::Kind` is {Overnight, Term} and a price index fixed monthly, with a lag and seasonality, is neither. New conventions, new coupon mechanics, new blueprints. Note theirs is a STANDALONE problem too -- it reuses their solver but is not a member of their curve bundle, so this is not as entangled as it looks.
- **`Credit`** -- A second stochastic quantity (a survival/hazard curve) multiplying every discount factor, and a protection leg integrating over default time. Our `df(slot, t)` callable generalises; nothing else does. Theirs is one row shape only (no accrual-on-default, no index or tranche), so the target is smaller than the family name suggests.
- **`Bonds, RV and asset swaps`** -- Cheapest of the absent families: the coupon mechanics are largely `CouponKind::Fixed` already, so it is a redemption cashflow, a clean/dirty price quote convention and a bond blueprint. Their family selector is `derive::GovvieModel { Spline, NelsonSiegel, Svensson }` (`derive/bond_rv.hpp:83`), and the parametric two need curve forms `curve::SchemeKind` does not have.
- **`FX: spot, forward, options, NDF`** -- The same Stage B blocker for the linear part. Their FX options and NDFs are stateless, bundle-free verbs taking {spot, r_dom, r_for} directly, so they are not even curve consumers -- a separate pricing surface rather than a calibration one.
- **`Rates and FX volatility`** -- Entirely outside this engine's scope today: a vol surface, an option payoff and a second stochastic driver. Eight headers on their side. Nothing on ours -- `Op::` has no normal CDF and the recorded world has no optionality beyond `Op::Select`. Not a near-term coverage item at any price.
- **`XVA / exposure`** -- **Their weakest row, and worth knowing before planning against it**: the header is ~60 lines, delivers EPE/ENE/PFE only, and computes no CVA, DVA, FVA, MVA or KVA anywhere. Its curve-state proxy is described in their own source as illustrative pending a calibrated LGM/HW1F. Comparing here would measure very little.
- **`VaR / ES`** -- A thin layer on top of a capability we have: it is a quantile over many repriced scenarios, and Stage A already recalibrates its whole scenario set. What is missing is only the distribution and quantile step -- no new maths in the recorded world at all. The cheapest absent row on this axis by a wide margin.

**What it would take**, for the *theirs only* rows:

- **`CSA / collateral`** -- Nothing here: `grep -ri csa|collateral` over `include/epykos/` and `src/` finds zero hits. Mechanically it is a per-trade choice of discount curve, which `Leg::disc_curve` already expresses, so the cost is a trade field and a blueprint field, not new maths. Worth knowing theirs is partial too: `threshold`, `mta`, `independent_amount` and `rounding` are declared and consumed nowhere, and `Uncollateralized` is unreachable from their JSON wire. So the comparable part of this row is just the discount-curve choice.
- **`Turns / year-end jumps`** -- See `TurnJump` on axis 1: a state-vector extension plus an overlay term, not a new `curve::SchemeKind`. Their turn deltas are deliberately excluded from the curvature regulariser and from the parallel-shift direction, which is a design detail we would have to reproduce rather than discover.
- **`Regularisation / smoothing`** -- Deliberately outside the comparison today, and that is not an accident: `fixtures::compare_ois` is SQUARE by construction (one knot per instrument) precisely so neither engine needs a regulariser the two would not share. Needed the moment the calibration is over- or under-determined -- so this row cannot become *compared* without first choosing to make the comparison non-square.
- **`P&L explain`** -- **Cheaper than the name suggests, and cheaper than a first reading of it concluded.** Theirs is FIRST order: carry (numeraire rebased to t1), roll-down (cashflows slid down an unchanged curve), market (the analytic delta ladder dotted with the quote move) and a residual term that absorbs the rest -- no bump-and-reprice and no second derivative. We already have the analytic ladder (O3, the head-to-head's own target), so this needs the carry and roll-down terms and an attribution identity, NOT the gamma that `Dual<N>` over hardcoded `double` forecloses. It is not blocked behind I2.
- **`Cross-basis risk transform`** -- A distinct capability from the ladder above, and we do not have it: theirs re-levels one bundle's quotes onto another's, re-solves and re-expresses the risk, with NPV and parallel DV01 as invariants. We hold the pieces -- `J_z` is already built lazily at the solution (D85/D89) -- so this is a matrix solve between two quote bases rather than new recorded maths.
- **`External oracle`** -- We have D2's templated-`double` path as an INTERNAL oracle, which catches a recording bug but **cannot catch a convention bug, because it is the same conventions code**. The front stub disagreement in `bench/compare/README.md` is exactly that class of bug. One detail that is easy to get backwards: their QuantLib is **mandatory by default**, not an opt-in gated build -- the CMake option is `SWAPS_ALLOW_NO_ORACLE` and it opts OUT (absence is otherwise a FATAL_ERROR), and their shipped core and API link no QuantLib at all; only their oracle and bench targets do. Adding one here needs a D12 dependency decision.
- **`Soft quotes / bands`** -- Changes the residual itself rather than the maths around it, so for us it is a residual wrapper -- the same missing degree of freedom as `Npv` and `Portfolio`. It is how their turn deltas stay identifiable, which is why it is not independent of the turns row.
- **`Streaming / incremental recalibration`** -- Our nearest thing is the warm re-quote path the head-to-head already times (D85/D89's lazy final Jacobian), which is a warm re-solve but not a frozen-Newton stream with a staleness bound, and we have no background refresh. Partially reachable, and the measurement half of it is already in place.

#### Interpolation schemes, overlap computed rather than asserted

`curve::SchemeKind` live: **6** (`flat`, `linear`, `hermite`, `natural_cubic`, `monotone_cubic`, `bspline`). Theirs, snapshot: **8** (`curve::Scheme`, their `kSchemeCount = 8`).

| | schemes |
|---|---|
| both | **6** -- `bspline`, `flat`, `hermite`, `linear`, `monotone_cubic`, `natural_cubic` |
| theirs only | **2** -- `monotone_convex`, `tension` |
| ours only | **0** -- none |

So the interpolation families are **not** a coverage gap: 6 of their 8 are ours too, and the two they have that we do not (`monotone_convex`, `tension`) are both value-dependent forms. What *is* narrow is use, not capability -- only 2 of our 6 appear in a curve definition today, and the head-to-head deliberately pins one.

`curve::Variable` live: **3** (`zero`, `logdf`, `forward`); used by a curve definition today: `logdf`, `zero`. Schemes used by a curve definition today: `linear`, `monotone_cubic`.
Their extrapolation is a fixed flat policy with no enum, so there is nothing to compare there.

## 4. The gap that costs nothing to close: Stage A against the head-to-head

Both columns are generated -- Stage A from `blueprints/problems/stage_a.json` through
`fixtures::load_stage_a_definition`, the head-to-head by building `fixtures::compare_ois`
with its default options and looking at what came out.

| | Stage A (our own problem) | head-to-head (`compare_ois`) |
|---|---|---|
| curves | 4 (+ 3 scheme variants) | 1 |
| currencies | 2 | 1 |
| trades | 2000 | 64 |
| trade blueprints in the mix | 8 | 1 |
| instrument kinds in the book | 3 -- `basis`, `irs`, `ois` | 1 -- `ois` |
| coupon mechanics | 4 -- `fixed`, `rfr_averaged`, `rfr_compounded`, `term_rate` | 2 -- `fixed`, `rfr_compounded` |
| instrument kinds in the CALIBRATION set | 5 -- `basis`, `deposit`, `future`, `irs`, `ois` | 1 -- `ois` |
| calibration instruments | 70 across 4 curves | 16 on 16 knots (square) |
| netting sets | 40 | 0 |
| seasoned fraction | 20% | 0 |
| realised fixings in the history | generated from the seed, daily from the definition's start date | 0 -- empty by construction |
| curve schemes exercised | `linear`, `monotone_cubic` | `linear` |
| curve variables exercised | `logdf`, `zero` | `logdf` |
| scenarios | 1000 over 4 families (`parallel`, `twist`, `butterfly`, `per_curve`) | -- |

**Confirmed: Stage A is far richer than the head-to-head uses.** 4 curves against 1, 2 currencies against 1, 2000 trades against 64, 8 trade blueprints against 1, 40 netting sets against none, and 20% seasoned against a fixings history that is empty by
construction. The book-side kinds alone go 1 -> 3 and the coupon mechanics 2 -> 4.

**One thing the generated table says that a hand-written one would have got wrong: Stage A's
BOOK and its CALIBRATION SET are different surfaces.** The book draws from 8 blueprints covering 3 instrument kinds (`basis`, `irs`, `ois`) over 4 coupon mechanics; the calibration set covers 5 (`basis`, `deposit`, `future`, `irs`, `ois`).
So `deposit` and `future` are already exercised by Stage A -- on the calibration side, where
a quote kind actually lives -- even though no trade in the book is one. That makes the
`Rate` row on axis 1 cheaper than the book column alone suggests, and it is why item 1 of
section 6 is a fixture change and not a product change.

### But the restrictions are not all accidental, and a plan has to respect the difference

`include/epykos/fixtures/compare_ois.hpp`'s own header gives four reasons for the narrowing,
and they are of two different kinds:

- **Fixture narrowness** -- cheap to widen, nothing defends it: one curve, one currency, one
  instrument type; no seasoned trades.
- **Deliberate agreement control** -- *not* cheap, and widening it would damage the
  comparison rather than improve it:
  - the curve is `linear`/`logdf` so the **interpolation scheme is removed from the
    comparison** instead of being assumed shared (D71 measured that their bundle curve is
    the same family);
  - the calibration is **square**, one knot per instrument, so neither side needs a
    pseudo-inverse or a regulariser the two would not share;
  - `max_start_offset_days` defaults to **0 because the two engines disagree on front
    stubs** -- measured, at 360 days the book NPV and the ladder diverge by 1e-3..1e-4
    relative while the curve still agrees to 5.8e-13, which localises the difference to the
    stub and nothing else.

So "widen the head-to-head" splits into work that is nearly free and work that is blocked on
a convention disagreement. Section 6 keeps them apart. The fixture already carries
`max_start_offset_years`, which ages a trade by a whole number of years and therefore lands
on the same annual roll grid -- the stub-free way to add seasoning.

### Stage A has no FX -- confirmed, not assumed

Generated from the problem definition: every FX entry is a placeholder (`USD = 1`, `EUR = 1`), and placeholder-only is **true**.
The definition's own notes say the USD conversion of EUR values is a structure placeholder of
1.0 applied as a recorded product (`fx.placeholder`), and that **Stage B replaces it with an
FX spot input**. So `FxForward`, `XccyMtmBasis` and the FX and cross-currency families are
blocked on Stage B, not on a small change.

>
> A further **24%** (8 rows) we already support and simply do not exercise: reachable by widening a fixture,
> subject to the stub caveat. The remaining **65%** (22 rows) is capability we do not have.
>
> Put the other way: **35% of their surface is within reach of the engine as it stands**, and 65% is not.

Read the denominator honestly. It counts *their* rows, so it is a measure of their surface,
not of engineering merit: their volatility, XVA, bond and FX-option families are whole
product areas this engine has never claimed, and one of them (XVA) is thin on their side
too. The useful signal is the **24% supported-but-not-compared band**,
which is pure unrealised measurement, and the shape of the 65% -- how much of it is one missing degree of freedom rather than one missing product.

## 6. What would most widen the comparable surface, cheapest first

Ranked by comparable rows gained per unit of work, with *fixture* work (we have the
capability) separated from *capability* work (we do not).

### Fixture work -- the 24% already paid for

1. **Put a second and third instrument type in the head-to-head: `Deposit`, then `Basis`.**
   Pure fixture work. Both are already built, blueprinted and exercised by Stage A;
   `compare_ois` simply does not instantiate them. `Basis` buys `ParSpread` outright and
   `Deposit` buys most of `Rate` -- and `Rate` needs nothing else, because neither engine
   models convexity and theirs takes it as an input that can be set to zero. **Two axis-1
   rows, no engine change.** Cheapest real gain anywhere in this document.
2. **Widen the head-to-head to the multi-curve, two-currency case.** Fixture work, and the
   capability is there: Stage A already stacks 4 curves over 2 currencies with forecast != discount, and `CurveSet::Mode::joint`
   exists. **It does not need FX** -- two currencies' curves calibrate independently as long
   as nothing converts between them, which is exactly Stage A's position. Buys the
   multi-curve family row and strengthens the ladder row.
3. **Seasoned trades in the head-to-head, aged by whole years.** Capability is there
   (`FixingsHistory`, 20% of Stage A). Use
   `max_start_offset_years` rather than `max_start_offset_days`: whole-year ageing lands on
   the annual roll grid and so avoids the measured front-stub disagreement, which is the
   only reason this is not item 1.
4. **Netting sets and the scenario grid.** Both already exist on our side (40 sets, 1000 scenarios over 4 families in Stage A) and neither crosses the boundary today. Cheap, and the scenario row
   is the prerequisite for the VaR item below.

### Capability work -- cheapest first

5. **A quote-convention degree of freedom on a calibration instrument.** The single highest
   leverage change in this document: **four *theirs only* rows behind one structural
   change** -- `Npv` (the residual is `pv - target`, and `instrument::pv<Scalar>` already
   exists), `ZeroCouponRate` (`exp(log(1+tau*q)/tau)-1`, expressible in the current op set,
   no `Op::Pow` needed), `Portfolio` (a weighted sum of component residuals) and the
   soft-quote band. `CurveSet::add_instrument` already takes an arbitrary residual callable,
   so no engine maths changes. The one real wrinkle is that `Npv` is in PV units while every
   residual here is in rate units by design, so it also wants a per-instrument residual
   scale.
6. **VaR / ES.** A quantile over many repriced scenarios, and Stage A already recalibrates a
   full scenario set. No new recorded maths at all -- the distribution and quantile step is
   the whole of it. Cheapest absent row on axis 2 by a wide margin, and it rides on item 4.
7. **P&L explain.** Re-ranked upward after reading their implementation: theirs is **first
   order** -- carry, roll-down, the analytic delta ladder dotted with the quote move, and a
   residual term -- with no bump-and-reprice and no second derivative. We already have the
   analytic ladder; this needs the carry and roll-down terms and an attribution identity.
   **It is not blocked behind second order**, which is what a first reading of it suggested.
8. **CSA / collateral, as a trade-level discount choice.** Mechanically a per-trade choice of
   discount curve, which `Leg::disc_curve` already expresses, so the cost is a trade field
   and a blueprint field. And the comparable part is small: on their side the economic terms
   (threshold, MTA, independent amount, rounding) are declared and consumed nowhere.
9. **Cross-basis risk transform.** We already build `J_z` lazily at the solution (D85/D89),
   so re-expressing a ladder in a second quote basis is a matrix solve rather than new
   recorded maths.
10. **A bond blueprint.** Cheapest of the absent *families*: the coupon mechanics are largely
    `CouponKind::Fixed` already, so it is a redemption cashflow, a price quote convention and
    a blueprint -- and it unlocks their bond-fit and bond-universe rows together. The
    parametric fits (Nelson-Siegel, Svensson) are a separate curve form we do not have.
11. **An external oracle.** Lowest coverage gain, highest *trust* gain, and it should be read
    that way: our `double` oracle shares the conventions code with the engine, so it cannot
    catch a convention bug -- and the front-stub disagreement is precisely a convention bug.
    Needs a D12 dependency decision.
12. **Turns, then regularisation.** Turns are a state-vector extension plus a curve overlay
    (not a new scheme), which the IFT ladder and the adjoint both see, so it is not as local
    as it looks. Regularisation cannot become *compared* at all until the comparison is
    deliberately made non-square, since squareness is currently a feature of the fixture.
13. **Streaming / frozen-Newton recalibration.** Partially reachable: the warm re-solve the
    head-to-head already times is the nearest thing, but there is no staleness envelope and
    no background Jacobian refresh.
14. **FX spot, i.e. Stage B.** Gates `FxForward`, `XccyMtmBasis` and the FX and
    cross-currency families -- **4 rows, the largest single block** -- but it is a
    problem-stage change rather than a fixture change, which is why it sits here and not
    higher despite the row count.
15. **Inflation, then credit.** Each needs a new index type or a new stochastic quantity
    before any instrument exists. Note both are standalone problems on their side too, so
    neither has to join the curve bundle. Last on cost, not on value.
16. **Volatility, and XVA.** Volatility is out of scope at any near-term price: a vol
    surface, an option payoff and a second driver, with no normal CDF in the op set. XVA is
    ranked last for a different reason -- comparing against a ~60-line EPE/ENE/PFE header
    that computes no CVA or FVA would measure very little even if we built it.
